test_title: PYST 15: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 11 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which major discovery helps to design drugs in the treatment of hyperacidity?

options.text: The role of enzymes in digestion
The use of antibiotics to neutralize stomach acid
Hydrochloric acid present in the stomach
Histamine stimulates acid secretion in the stomach

solution:
The correct answer is __**Histamine stimulates acid secretion in the stomach**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Histamine plays a crucial role** in stimulating the secretion of gastric acid in the stomach by binding to H2 receptors on the parietal cells.
 
• This discovery has been instrumental in the development of **H2 receptor antagonists** such as ranitidine and famotidine, which are widely used to treat hyperacidity and related disorders.
 
• Histamine-mediated acid secretion is an important target in the treatment of conditions like **gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcers, and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome**.
 
• The regulation of histamine pathways has also led to advancements in **proton pump inhibitors (PPIs)**, which further reduce gastric acid production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Histamine:** A chemical messenger released by certain cells in the body, including mast cells, that plays a key role in immune responses and gastric acid secretion.
 
• **H2 Receptor Antagonists:** Drugs like ranitidine and cimetidine that block histamine H2 receptors, reducing stomach acid production and relieving symptoms of hyperacidity.
 
• **Proton Pump Inhibitors (PPIs):** Medications such as omeprazole and esomeprazole that inhibit the final step in acid secretion, providing long-lasting relief for acid-related conditions.
 
• **Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD):** A chronic condition where stomach acid frequently flows back into the esophagus, causing irritation and requiring acid-suppressing treatments.
 
• **Parietal Cells:** Specialized cells in the stomach lining that produce hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor, essential for digestion and vitamin B12 absorption.
